body:
Observed on a live two-lane `pdca flow` in the wyrd-pdca instance (2026-08-02): both bundles' Check reviewer leaves ran concurrently, each doing the independent re-verification `agents/reviewer.md` mandates (`template/agents/reviewer.md.jinja:24-25` — *"Re-run the asserted evidence: stash the fix → confirm red; unstash → confirm green … Trust re-runs, not claims"*). Between them they wrote ~69 GB of cold build trees in ~13 minutes. `systemd-oomd` then killed the **entire terminal cgroup** — driver, both lanes, both bundles:

```
systemd-oomd: Killed /user.slice/.../ptyxis-spawn-…scope due to memory pressure
  for user@1000.service being 75.72% > 50.00% for > 20s with reclaim activity
systemd: ptyxis-spawn-…scope: Consumed 2d 23h 39min CPU over 3d 19h 51min
  wall clock, 53.4G memory peak
```

Neither reviewer had written `check-review.md`; the run's whole Check band was lost.

Grepping `template/src/`, `template/agents/`, `template/engine/`, `template/scripts/` for `MemoryMax`, `systemd-run`, `rlimit`, `setrlimit`, `ulimit`, `cgroup`, `OOMPolicy` returns zero hits — leaves are spawned with no resource limit at all. Because oomd kills the *cgroup*, not the offender, the failure is also unattributable: it surfaces as the driver vanishing, with nothing in any gate log.

Suggested direction: an optional `[driver].leaf_memory_max` (with a per-leaf `[leaves.*].memory_max` override) that wraps the leaf argv in a capped transient scope where the facility exists, and is a documented no-op where it doesn't:

```
systemd-run --user --scope --quiet --collect \
  -p MemoryMax=<N> -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p OOMPolicy=continue -- <argv…>
```

`OOMPolicy=continue` is the load-bearing half — the kernel kills the offending subprocess *inside* the scope and the leaf survives to report, instead of oomd taking the session. And since a cgroup's `memory.current` counts page cache, the cap makes the leaf reclaim its own build cache rather than flooding system-wide page cache, which is what actually killed this run.

Prior art for the exact pattern, including this failure mode: wyrd's own `.github/workflows/mutants.yml:155-162`, whose comment describes an unbounded mutant run OOM-killing the runner *before* the per-mutant timeout can fire, surfacing as a spurious "operation was canceled".

Relation to #419: granting the reviewer a writable disposable clone/worktree is the right call, but it multiplies this footprint. A cap is the containment that makes that direction safe to adopt.

Template-vs-instance boundary: leaf process spawning is harness machinery (`leaves.py`), not instance config, hence filed here.
title: leaves: leaf subprocesses run unbounded — a building leaf takes the whole flow down with it
